en: You can also put Agents.md files
into subfolders in your project, like in the
source or even the components folder. And
you can also add such files there in
addition to that root Agents.md file.
So here I added a second Agents.md file in
that components folder in addition to the
root Agents.md file. And then you could put
specific instructions in there that apply to
what's going on in this folder. Like for
example, components must start with a
capital character, which doesn't make too
much sense. That's a general React rule, but
it's just an example.
However, for this agents.md file to be
picked up, you must make sure that the Codex
session that should respect it is started in
that folder. So we would have to navigate
into that components folder and then start
Codex from in there.
In the native app, you would add a new
project and point at that source components
folder.
That's how this agents.md file would be
picked up.
Now here I don't need that, but it's worth
knowing about this, especially of course
when working within monorepos. That can be
useful for having a general agents.md file
and then some specific files. Worth noting
is that the general file will always be
applied and additional nested files are
applied in addition to it but can override
it. So for clashing instructions, the more
nested ones should win.
